svg.title: The extraction pipeline inside one tools/call, and the cache short-circuit
svg.desc: A client call to browse_url crosses a dashed tool boundary and meets the page cache first, a lookup bounded by a ten minute time to live and a hundred entries with the oldest evicted. On a hit the call turns right into a short-circuit box that sets from_cache true, and a long rail carries it straight down the right-hand side to the result without touching anything in between. On a miss the call continues down the spine: a Chromium navigation with a half second settle that then reads the rendered document back, noted as one browser per process and one page per call closed in a finally block; then extract, which tries trafilatura for articles with precision favoured, falls back to markdownify with the unwanted elements removed from the tree rather than stripped, and reports empty when nothing rendered; then a write back into the cache. The two byte counts the hero figure is drawn from are marked on the stages that produce them, 76,201 bytes into the render and 4,126 bytes out of the extractor. Both paths meet at one result box carrying the page content and its receipt of raw bytes, clean bytes and method, which travels back up the left-hand rail and out across the boundary to the client. A closing line states that a hit returns at the tool boundary, paying for no navigation and no extraction.
svg.text: All of this is one tools/call. The cache decides how much of it runs.
A hit returns at the tool boundary. No navigation, no extraction, and from_cache says so in the result.
